questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: The compartment of the fowl's stomach that corresponds with the true stomach of a ruminant farm animal:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Proventriculus (2 marks)
The proventriculus is the glandular stomach of a fowl, where gastric juices (hydrochloric acid and enzymes) are secreted. It corresponds functionally with the abomasum (true stomach) of a ruminant.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following statements applies to a ration that has 10 parts of maize meal and three parts of fishmeal:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Has a higher percentage of maize meal than fish meal (2 marks)
10 parts maize meal out of 13 total parts (about 77%) is more than 3 parts fish meal (about 23%).

options.A: Has a higher percentage of fish meal than maize meal
options.B: Has a higher percentage of maize meal than fish meal
options.C: Has equal percentages of maize meal and fish meal
options.D: Has 10% maize meal and 70% fish meal

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper shows a bolus of food inside the oesophagus, with an arrow showing it being moved downwards by the surrounding muscle. The diagram shows the process where each of the following occurs:
(i) The muscles above the bolus contract to push the food downwards.
(ii) The muscles below the bolus relax to move the food upwards.
(iii) The muscles constantly contract and relax to move the food down the oesophagus.
(iv) The muscles below the bolus relax to move the food downwards.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
This describes peristalsis: circular muscles contract behind (above) the bolus and relax in front of (below) the bolus, and this wave of alternating contraction and relaxation moves the food downwards. Statement (ii) is wrong because the food moves downwards, not upwards.

subQuestions.questionText: The following is the CORRECT sequence of the process of rumination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Regurgitation → reinsalivation → re-chewing → re-swallowing (2 marks)
During rumination, coarse feed is brought back up from the rumen (regurgitation), mixed again with saliva (reinsalivation), chewed again (re-chewing) and swallowed again (re-swallowing).

subQuestions.questionText: A facility used to restrain cattle during dehorning:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Crush (2 marks)
A crush is a narrow, strongly built passage (usually with a head clamp) that holds an animal firmly still for procedures such as dehorning, vaccination and pregnancy testing.

subQuestions.questionText: The following is a sign of stress in cattle:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Pawing (2 marks)
Pawing (scraping the ground with a front hoof) is a sign of stress/agitation in cattle. Snout rubbing, belly nibbling and cannibalism are abnormal behaviours associated mainly with pigs and poultry.

subQuestions.questionText: Diseases that are caused by mineral deficiencies:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Non-infectious (2 marks)
Deficiency diseases are non-infectious because they are not caused by a pathogen and cannot be spread from one animal to another.

subQuestions.questionText: Parasites, especially in sheep, that are responsible for the irritation of the sinuses, causing sneezing and a discharge of a yellowish mucus:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Nasal worms (2 marks)
Nasal worm (Oestrus ovis, actually the sheep nasal bot fly larva, commonly grouped with nasal worms) larvae live in the nasal passages and sinuses of sheep, causing irritation, sneezing and a yellowish nasal discharge.

subQuestions.questionText: The primary sex organ of a bull:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Testis (2 marks)
The testis is the primary (essential) sex organ / gonad of the bull because it produces the gametes (sperm) and the male sex hormone (testosterone). The scrotum, penis and urethra are accessory/secondary structures.

subQuestions.questionText: … are female sex hormones responsible for the contraction of the uterine muscles.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Oxytocin and oestrogen (2 marks)
Oxytocin and oestrogen both stimulate contraction of the uterine (myometrial) muscles, e.g. during oestrus and parturition. Progesterone has the opposite effect (it keeps the uterus relaxed during pregnancy).

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A. Write A only, B only, both A and B or none.
COLUMN A: A: Rectum; B: Caecum
COLUMN B: The enlarged first part of the large intestine in pigs where absorption of water occurs
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
The caecum is the enlarged blind pouch at the start of the large intestine, where water and volatile fatty acids are absorbed. The rectum is the last part of the large intestine, where faeces are stored.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Pearson square; B: Feed square
COLUMN B: Method of balancing the rations to determine the required protein value in a feed mixture
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A only (2 marks)
The Pearson square (Pearson's square) is the method used to balance two feeds to obtain a required protein percentage in the mixture. 'Feed square' is not a recognised method.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Large-scale production system; B: Modern farming system
COLUMN B: A farming system that produces food, mainly to feed the family
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Producing food mainly to feed the family is subsistence farming. Both a large-scale production system and a modern farming system are commercial systems aimed at producing a surplus for sale.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Ointments; B: Anthelmintics
COLUMN B: Chemicals that kill ticks and mites
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Chemicals that kill ticks and mites are acaricides. Ointments are topical medicated pastes; anthelmintics are remedies against internal worms.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Artificial vagina; B: Electro-ejaculator
COLUMN B: Apparatus used in the process of collecting semen from a bull
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Both the artificial vagina and the electro-ejaculator are apparatus used to collect semen from a bull.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The absorption of volatile fatty acids along the concentration gradient through the rumen wall.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Passive absorption / diffusion (2 marks)
Movement of a substance along (down) a concentration gradient, without the use of energy, is passive absorption (diffusion).

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A preventative measure whereby farm animals with a contagious disease are kept away from healthy animals.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Quarantine / isolation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The hormone which inhibits milk ejection when a cow is in a scary and unusual situation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Adrenalin (adrenaline / epinephrine) (2 marks)
When a cow is frightened, adrenalin is released and blocks the action of oxytocin, inhibiting milk let-down (ejection).

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A milky, sticky, creamy and opaque liquid released through the penis during ejaculation.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Semen (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A thin-walled elastic tube that extends from the urethral opening to the vulva.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Vagina (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Proper protein supplies the required amount and proportion of all amino acids.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Ideal / complete / egg (protein) (1 mark)
An ideal (complete) protein supplies all the essential amino acids in the correct amount and proportion.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
An elastrator is a castration tool used in farm animals and causes bleeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Knife / scalpel / (surgical) castration (1 mark)
Castration with a knife/scalpel causes bleeding. An elastrator (rubber ring method) is a bloodless method of castration.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The allantois is the outer germ layer from which the external organs, mainly the skin, hooves and hair, develop.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Ectoderm (1 mark)
The ectoderm is the outer germ layer that forms the skin, hooves, hair and nervous system. The allantois is a foetal membrane.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Artificial insemination takes place when the bull is allowed to mount and service a cow.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Mating / copulation / natural service (1 mark)
When a bull mounts and serves a cow directly, it is natural mating (copulation). Artificial insemination is the mechanical placement of semen into the cow's tract.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Meiosis is the division of diploid spermatogonium to become larger.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Mitosis (1 mark)
During the multiplication and growth phases of spermatogenesis the diploid spermatogonia divide by mitosis (and enlarge into primary spermatocytes). Meiosis only occurs later, in the maturation phase.

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper (labelled A, B and C) show close-up views of the inner lining of the parts of the stomach in a farm animal: Picture A has many long, leaf-like folds; Picture B is densely covered with large tongue-shaped papillae; Picture C has a raised honeycomb / net-like pattern.
Name the farm animal with the stomach parts represented in the pictures above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Cattle / sheep / goat (any ruminant) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the letter of the stomach part where EACH of the following occurs:
(a) Foreign objects accumulate
(b) Heat is produced
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) C (1 mark) – the reticulum (honeycomb lining), where heavy/sharp foreign objects (wire, nails) settle
(b) B (1 mark) – the rumen (large papillae), where microbial fermentation produces heat

subQuestions.questionText: The farm animal with stomach parts A, B and C above can survive on feed low in fat-soluble vitamins. Justify this statement by indicating the adaptation feature and its role.
subQuestions.memoText: The stomach (rumen) contains micro-organisms ✓ (adaptation feature) that are able to synthesise vitamins ✓ (role), so the animal does not depend entirely on vitamins in the feed. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Use the letters of the stomach parts to indicate the sequence with which the feed will flow after regurgitation.
subQuestions.memoText:
B → C → A (1 mark for each letter in the correct position)
After regurgitation and re-chewing, the finer feed is re-swallowed and passes from the rumen (B) to the reticulum (C) and then to the omasum (A).

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are the symptoms of nutrient deficiencies in farm animals:
A: Deformation and ulceration of the cornea in the eye
B: Porous bones, especially in older animals
C: Bad sores on the skin
D: Paleness of the mucous membrane
E: Enlarged thyroid gland
Identify the mineral that is deficient in C and D.
subQuestions.memoText:
C - Zinc / Zn (1 mark) – zinc deficiency causes skin lesions/sores (parakeratosis)
D - Iron / Fe (1 mark) – iron deficiency causes anaemia, seen as pale mucous membranes

subQuestions.questionText: Name the deficiency symptoms shown by the farm animals in B and E.
subQuestions.memoText:
B - Osteomalacia / porous (soft) bones (1 mark)
E - Goitre / enlarged thyroid gland (iodine deficiency) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Classify the vitamin that causes the deficiency in A according to its grouping.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Fat-soluble vitamin (1 mark)
Symptom A (corneal deformation and ulceration) is caused by a vitamin A deficiency, and vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO methods of supplementing the vitamin that is deficient in A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Injection (of vitamin A)
• Dosing / a water-based vitamin A mixed with the drinking water
• Supplementing the ration (adding vitamin A to the feed)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the results of a digestibility co-efficiency trial conducted with two different farm animals that consumed wheat straw:
ANIMAL A: Dry matter intake 15 kg; Dry matter excreted 13 kg; Digestibility coefficient 13%
ANIMAL B: Dry matter intake 15 kg; Dry matter excreted 5 kg; Digestibility coefficient 67%
Identify the type of farm animal used as A.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Non-ruminant / monogastric farm animal (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• The feed was less digested / low digestibility coefficient
• The stomach of the animal is not adapted to digest crude fibre / it has a simple stomach
• Only 13% (2 kg) of the feed was digested and 87% (13 kg) was excreted

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO factors that might have influenced the digestibility of the feed used in the trial.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Type / composition of the feed
• Type of animal
• Individuality of the animal
• Preparation of the feed
• Age of the animal
• Age of the plant
• Quantity of feed consumed

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO methods of improving the digestibility of this feed (wheat straw).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Pelleting
• Supplementing / mixing with additives / molasses / urea / ammonification
• Grinding (milling)

subQuestions.questionText:
The information below shows the composition of a feed:
Carbohydrates 55%; Digestible protein (DP) 15%; Fats 5%; Total digestible nutrients (TDN) not given.
Calculate the nutritive ratio (NR) of the feed. Show ALL calculations, including the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – TDN = 55% + 15% + 5% = 75% ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2 – Formula: NR = 1 : (%TDN − %DP) ÷ %DP ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Substitution: = 1 : (75% − 15%) ÷ 15% ✓ (1 mark)
Step 4 – Answer: = 1 : 4 ✓ (1 mark)
(OR using DNNS = 75% − 15% = 60%; NR = 1 : 60 ÷ 15 = 1 : 4)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the suitability of the feed based on the nutritive ratio in QUESTION 2.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Suitable for growth / production / reproduction (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.4.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• The feed is high in protein
• It has a narrow nutritive ratio / narrower than 1 : 6

subQuestions.questionText:
The illustration in the question paper is a schematic representation of energy flow: Gross energy 1 000 kJ → (A) [energy lost in faeces = 150 kJ] → Metabolic energy 800 kJ [energy lost in urine and gases = 50 kJ] → (C) 550 kJ [energy lost in heat production = (B)] → Function (D) and For maintenance.
Name the energy in C.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Net energy / NE (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the function represented by D.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Production / growth / reproduction / work (1 mark)
(Net energy is used for maintenance plus production – growth, reproduction, milk, work.)

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the following based on the schematic representation above:
(a) Energy in A
(b) The amount of energy lost in B
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Energy in A = Gross energy − energy lost in faeces = 1 000 kJ − 150 kJ ✓ = 850 kJ ✓ (2 marks)
(b) Energy lost in B = Metabolic energy − net energy = 800 kJ − 550 kJ ✓ = 250 kJ ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO aims of calculating the energy value of a feed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• To determine the animal's diet
• To determine the feeding standards
• To determine the ration formulation

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows expected growth rates of farm animals as the temperature changes:
Temperature 35 °C: Cows 110 kg; Pigs 130 kg
Temperature 25 °C: Cows 100 kg; Pigs 90 kg
Temperature 15 °C: Cows 90 kg; Pigs 50 kg
Temperature 5 °C: Cows 80 kg; Pigs 25 kg
Temperature 0 °C: Cows 70 kg; Pigs 5 kg
Identify, in the table above, the farm animals that need to be kept in an environment with housing facilities.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pigs (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason, using data from the table above, to support the answer to QUESTION 3.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (2 marks):
• The growth rate of pigs shows a substantial decrease ✓ with a slight decrease in temperature ✓
• The growth rate of pigs shows a substantial increase ✓ with a slight increase in temperature ✓
(Pigs are very sensitive to temperature, so they need housing that controls the environment.)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a line graph to compare the growth rate of cows and pigs under different temperatures.
subQuestions.memoText:
A line graph with two lines (Cows and Pigs) of growth rate against temperature.

MARKING CRITERIA (1 mark each):
• Correct heading (e.g. 'Growth rate of cows and pigs at different temperatures')
• X-axis: correctly calibrated and labelled (Temperature, °C)
• Y-axis: correctly calibrated and labelled (Growth rate, kg)
• Line graph (two lines with a key)
• Correct units (kg and °C)
• Accuracy (at least 80% of points correctly plotted)

Points to plot:
• Cows: (0 °C, 70), (5 °C, 80), (15 °C, 90), (25 °C, 100), (35 °C, 110)
• Pigs: (0 °C, 5), (5 °C, 25), (15 °C, 50), (25 °C, 90), (35 °C, 130)

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is a list of equipment used in a broiler production unit: foldable curtains; electric heaters; fans on the roof and walls; insulation material on the roof.
Indicate the equipment in the list above that is used for EACH of the following situations:
(a) Keeping the temperature inside the broiler unit constant day and night
(b) Increasing the temperature inside during a sudden drop in environmental temperature
(c) Reducing the temperature on a very hot day
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Insulation material on the roof (1 mark)
(b) Electric heaters (1 mark)
(c) Fans on the roof and walls / foldable curtains (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper (labelled A and B) show different intensive chicken production systems: Picture A shows a large mobile chicken house standing in a field with many hens ranging freely on pasture around it; Picture B shows a small home coop with a few hens and a person feeding them in a yard.
Identify the type of intensive chicken production system in A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
PICTURE A - Free range (1 mark)
PICTURE B - Backyard (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors leading to increased production in the production systems above, other than nutrition.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Environment (housing, temperature, ventilation, lighting)
• Reproduction / breeding (genetically superior stock)
• General enterprise management

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the farm animals to which the following basic guideline applies when they are handled:
Carry them by both legs.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Chicken / poultry / fowl (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the farm animals to which the following basic guideline applies when they are handled:
Catch them above the joint of the hind legs.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Sheep / goat (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the farm animals to which the following basic guideline applies when they are handled:
Use a plywood board when moving them.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pigs (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph in the question paper indicates the seasonal trends in the occurrence of parasites that vary with regard to season and management. Parasite infestation (low to high) is plotted against season (Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall). The solid line is low in winter, rises through spring to a peak in summer and falls again in autumn. Two dashed reference lines are shown: a high line labelled 'possible (poor herd management)' and a low line labelled 'possible (good herd management)'.
Identify the season with the highest parasite infestation.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Summer (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE possible reason for the increase in the parasite infestation during the season identified in QUESTION 3.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Conducive (warm, moist) environmental conditions for parasites to breed
• Poor herd management

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO economic impacts of parasites.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Stock losses (deaths)
• Loss of production / reproduction
• Degrading of carcasses
• Increased production costs
• Loss of income / profit

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO good herd management practices that could have led to a lower parasite infestation during the autumn months.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Adequate feeding
• A well-planned health programme / chemical / biological control
• Avoiding breeding places of parasites / wet areas
• Practising rotational grazing
• Avoiding keeping animals in infested pens
• Good, clean / hygienic practices
• Creating an environment for natural enemies
• Using / selecting / breeding more resistant animals
• Burning of veld and pasture fields

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams in the question paper illustrate the life cycle of two different parasites. Diagram A shows a cycle between a human, a cow grazing on pasture and eggs/cysts passed out and picked up again. Diagram B shows a cycle between a sheep, grass, a water snail and stages labelled A to F.
Classify the parasite in B.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Internal / endo-parasite (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the parasites that are represented in A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
DIAGRAM A - Tapeworm (1 mark)
DIAGRAM B - Liver fluke / fluke worm (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO biological measures that can be used to control the parasite in B (liver fluke).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Creating an environment for natural enemies (of the snail host)
• Introduction of dung beetles / micro-fungi
• Breeding parasite-resistant animals

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows different symptoms of diseases affecting farm animals:
ANIMAL 1: Bleeds from the mouth, nose and anus
ANIMAL 2: Urinates dark red urine, has pale to yellow eyes and is later diagnosed with anaemia
Name the diseases affecting animal 1 and animal 2 respectively.
subQuestions.memoText:
ANIMAL 1 - Anthrax (1 mark)
ANIMAL 2 - Redwater (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the animal suffering from a deadly bacterial disease.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Animal 1 (anthrax is caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the animal with a non-infectious disease.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Animal 2 (1 mark)
(Redwater is not spread by direct contact between animals – it requires a tick vector – so it is classified here as non-infectious/non-contagious.)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the specific vector responsible for the transmission of the disease in animal 2.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Blue tick (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Match the following accessory sex glands with the description below. Choose from: Cowper's glands; prostate; seminal vesicles.
Surrounds the urethra at the neck of the bladder.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Prostate (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Match the following accessory sex glands with the description below. Choose from: Cowper's glands; prostate; seminal vesicles.
Located at the base of the penis on either side of the urethra and secrete an alkaline fluid that cleans the urethra.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Cowper's glands (bulbo-urethral glands) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Match the following accessory sex glands with the description below. Choose from: Cowper's glands; prostate; seminal vesicles.
Secretes a sticky yellowish fluid that provides energy to the sperm cells.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Seminal vesicle (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper illustrate a part of the reproductive system (Picture A) and a gamete (Picture B). In Picture A (a female reproductive system) label 1 points to a follicle bursting from the ovary, label 2 points to a site in the oviduct, D is a bracket across the ovary, and B points to the fluid surrounding a foetus developing in the uterus. In Picture B (a single sperm cell) F is the cap covering the front of the head, G is the head, H is the long whip-like tail and I is the short section between the head and the tail.
Identify the following:
(a) Part I in picture B
(b) Part H in picture B
(c) The process taking place at 1
(d) The process taking place at 2
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Part I - Mid piece (1 mark)
(b) Part H - Tail (1 mark)
(c) Process at 1 - Ovulation (1 mark)
(d) Process at 2 - Fertilisation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the hormone responsible for the process at 1 (ovulation) to take place.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Luteinising hormone / LH (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE function of structure D (the ovary).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Produces the female gametes / egg cells / ova (oogenesis)
• Produces the female sex hormones (oestrogen and progesterone)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE function of fluid B in picture A (the amniotic fluid).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Protects the embryo from injuries / acts as a shock absorber
• Hydration / prevents dehydration / prevents drying out of the foetus
• Lubricates the birth canal during parturition
• Thermoregulation (keeps the foetus at a constant temperature)
• Prevents the embryo from attaching to other tissues

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how part F enables the cell in picture B to penetrate the ovum.
subQuestions.memoText: Part F (the acrosome) releases an enzyme ✓ that breaks down / digests the wall (zona pellucida) of the ovum so that the sperm cell can enter ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the process that leads to the formation of the cell in picture B (the sperm cell).
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Spermatogenesis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Artificial insemination (AI) improves the conception rate in cows. To achieve the expected objective, the farmer needs to observe the signs of oestrus in order to detect heat.
Name the phase of the oestrus cycle during which artificial insemination could be performed.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Oestrus / met-oestrus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO methods that dairy farmers could use to detect heat in cows.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Chin ball marker
• Tail chalking
• Heat mount / watching detectors
• Heat observation (watching for standing heat, mucus discharge, restlessness)
• Pedometer
• Good record keeping
• The use of teaser animals

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO characteristics of good quality semen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Opaque / milky in colour
• Sticky
• Less than 15% dead sperm cells
• No deformed sperm cells / deformities
• No blood in the semen
• Healthy sperm cells
• Viable sperm cells
• High concentration of sperm cells

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of artificial insemination.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Spread of diseases if the semen is not tested
• An inexperienced / unskilled operator may cause damage
• Decreased genetic variation
• Some heifers are difficult to inseminate successfully
• May not give the desirable results
• Higher management demands
• Undesirable traits / congenital defects may be transferred to more offspring
• Labour intensive
• Time consuming
• Expensive procedure
• Difficult under extensive production systems

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph in the question paper shows different reproductive processes that occur in a dairy cow, over 12 months. Curve A (milk production, kg per day) rises from the start of milk production to a peak at about month 2 (marked 'Successful mating') and then declines steadily until the cow dries off at about month 9. A second curve shows the weight of the foetus (kg) staying low from about month 3 to month 9 ('Slow growth of foetus') and then rising steeply to month 12 ('Foetus grows very fast'). Bracket B spans the whole period and bracket C spans about month 3 to month 9.
Identify curve A.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Lactation curve (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Deduce the following from the graph above:
(a) The reproductive process from month 3 to 12
(b) The stage of the process in QUESTION 4.4.2(a) between month 9 and 12
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Pregnancy / gestation (1 mark)
(b) Foetal stage (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the month when the reproductive process in QUESTION 4.4.2(a) normally ends.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Month 12 (1 mark)
(Gestation in a cow is about 9 months from mating at month 2–3, so pregnancy ends at about month 12 with calving.)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO causes of abortion.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Malnutrition
• Injuries
• Hormonal disturbances / stress conditions
• Toxins / poisonous substances / laxatives / allergies / clovers high in oestrogen / immunisation of pregnant animals
• Diseases / infections / high fever
• Multiple births
• Genetic factors
• Transportation / moving of pregnant animals
• Embryo abnormalities

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason why it is necessary for pregnant lactating cows to dry off before the next lactation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• To allow the tissues in the mammary gland to recover
• To store body reserves / to prepare for the next lactation
• To supply the foetus with nutrients

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below represents three different techniques used in animal reproduction:
1: Cows are treated with hormones to come into oestrus at approximately the same time.
2: As many as possible embryos are taken from selected female animals after fertilisation.
3: The nucleus of a cell is removed and placed into another prepared egg cell.
Name the reproductive techniques numbered 1, 2 and 3.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 - Synchronisation of oestrus (1 mark)
2 - Embryo transfer / ET / multiple ovulation and embryo transfer (1 mark)
3 - Cloning / nuclear transfer (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO hormones that are used in technique 1 to achieve the intended results.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Prostaglandin
• Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
• Progestin (synthetic progesterone)
• Oestradiol
• MGA / melengestrol acetate

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO female animals involved in technique 2 (embryo transfer).
subQuestions.memoText:
• Donor / superior cow (1 mark)
• Recipient / inferior / surrogate cow (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the aim of technique 3 (cloning).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• To preserve / revive endangered species
• Rapid increase of animals with superior genetic traits
• For medical reasons
• To preserve and extend superior genes
• To create a replica / genetically identical organisms
